# DeltaFlow Volume Profile [BigBeluga]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

DeltaFlow Volume Profile adds a candle-direction decomposition to a recent-range volume profile. It aims to show both where volume clustered and whether candles assigned to each area leaned bullish or bearish. Its delta labels are derived from this candle-direction split, which is useful context but does not identify the aggressor of each trade or prove which participant dominated.

- Divide a lookback range into bins and aggregate volume, separating it by bullish/bearish candle direction.
- Normalize the component volumes into percentages and subtract bear percentage from bull percentage for bin delta.

# BE-Indicator Aggregator toolkit

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Evaluate user-authored combinations of external indicator plots and summarize historical trade outcomes. This toolkit is a small condition language and simulated trade evaluator, rather than an independent source of market signals.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Explicit comparison/Boolean setup evaluator is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- The caller connects external plots, declares variables, writes long/short conditions and supplies stop/target settings. Comment lines are ignored; prefixed lines identify variables or directional conditions.
- Pipe-separated criteria compare inputs, constants or lagged series. Operators cover comparisons, ranges, missing values and crosses; logical groups combine all/any conditions or minimum counts. Temporal conditions test recent or persistent truth.
- Examples combine RSI and a signal indicator, or support/resistance interaction and later confirmation; they illustrate how the language expresses discretionary setups.
- On supplied OHLC/external series implement E(=),NE(!=),G(>),GE(>=),L(<),LE(<=) comparisons and AND,OR,NAND,NOR,ATLEAST:N/NATLEAST:N Boolean aggregation. L-O|E|L means open=low;S-AND:O|E|H, O|G|C means open=high AND open>close. Caller binds lagged inputs and conjunction across setup lines. Ambiguous operators/full parser and backtest fills/statistics remain excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Historical summarized accuracy and illustrated day/scalp/position outputs help inspect the caller’s selected rules.
- External repainting or lag changes propagate into the evaluation; the toolkit itself does not establish input integrity.
- Usable scope: Explicit comparison/Boolean setup evaluator. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Condition Builder text, external source connections and expected stop-loss/take-profit values.
- Syntax requires comma-space between criteria; variables precede conditions. Long, short and variable prefixes are L-, S- and VAR-.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Optimizing arbitrary combinations on the same history can overfit. Accuracy alone does not measure net expectancy.
- Cross, temporal and parser edge cases may affect reproducibility, especially simultaneous long/short rules.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Trade fill timing, simultaneous stop/target ordering, sizing/cost handling and complete parser/condition aggregation behavior are unspecified.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv, caller external indicator plot series, caller condition-language text and stop/target settings.

## Idea and objective

Williams Fractal Trailing Stops uses confirmed high and low fractals as moving protective references. Unlike a fixed confirmation convention, the user can choose how many bars establish a fractal. The indicator then trails those structural points and can switch between long and short orientation when price crosses the trail. ## Parameters and stated settings

- Asset defaults to the chart symbol and can be changed. The author recommends one-minute through four-hour charts and warns on higher timeframes.

- Daily open depends on session conventions. Relative-to-open direction does not measure volume conviction or independently predict settlement.

# Initial Balance Auction Intelligence by DGT

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Initial Balance Auction Intelligence follows how price behaves after an opening range, separating tentative probes from completed-window acceptance or failure. It layers retest continuation/rejection, session character and cumulative directional pressure over the basic IB references. The goal is auction context, explicitly not standalone signals or actual order-flow measurement.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** IB references and basic acceptance/failure is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Establish opening-session high/low/midpoint, then evaluate each completed post-IB window against those boundaries.
- Classify outside closes as accepted and beyond-boundary extensions closing inside as failed; track subsequent retest holds/failures and two-sided rejection.
- Accumulate bounded session pressure and grade event quality/maturity with additional price-structure criteria.
- Over caller initial-balance window take H=max(high),L=min(low),R=H-L,M=(H+L)/2. Project H+kR and L-kR for k=0.5,1,1.5. After completed IB,close outside H/L indicates acceptance;an outside excursion/extension followed by close back inside indicates failure under the source rule. Caller defines observation window/boundaries;pressure,quality,retest and advanced states excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Read dashboard regime/bias/phase/state/pressure/quality and invalidation together; confirmed state transitions support alerts, while live decision candles remain provisional.
- Usable scope: IB references and basic acceptance/failure. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Post-IB windows include 5/10/15/30 minutes; extension references use 0.5/1/1.5 times IB range. Pressure spans -100 to +100.
- Engine operates on intraday charts at most thirty minutes and uses one-minute data on larger intraday bars. Session/timezone are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: acceptance is a configured completed-window rule, not proof of durable market acceptance; projected extensions are expressly not guaranteed targets.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Quality/pressure/maturity formulas, retest tolerances, IB schedule defaults, regime transitions and invalidation calculations are not fully specified.

- The printed HMA branch calls SMA, so the family label contradicts supplied code. Exponentially amplified historical returns are weighting heuristics, not actual investable equity; non-repaint statements remain unverified.

# Volume Cluster Profile [VCP] (Zeiierman)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Build a cluster-smoothed volume-by-price map for the current lookback and prior pivot-to-pivot segments. The result emphasizes major concentrations and thin areas, providing discretionary reference zones rather than a literal record of all transactions at each price.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Nondegenerate current-window enhanced profile/POC is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Scan window extremes, split the range into bins, and assign each bar’s entire volume to its close-price bin. Select local histogram peaks at least as high as immediate neighbors and above average bin volume, retaining the strongest up to a cap.
- For each price bin, sum Gaussian contributions from cluster centers, then divide by the number of retained centers. The largest enhanced bin defines POC at its midpoint.
- Historical swing profiles are stored between pivots; the latest segment’s highest and lowest enhanced-volume bins can extend forward as VA/LV zones. These are extrema, not a conventional percentage value-area calculation.
- For window min/max and B bins,step=(max-min)/B;allocate entire bar volume to clamp(floor((close-min)/step),0,B-1). Retain local peaks>=immediate neighbors and>average bin volume,sorted strongest up to caller cap. Enhanced[b]=sum(centerV*exp(-(b-center)^2/(2*sigma^2)))/center_count. POC is midpoint of maximum enhanced bin. Require nonflat range,positive sigma,at least one center;ties/empty centers and historical pivot segments remain limitations.

## Outputs and intended use

- Current/historical profiles, POC and projected zones support cluster-to-cluster rotation targets and acceptance/rejection observation.
- Single-cluster context is interpreted as bullish above, bearish below and balanced inside; these are author heuristics without a quantified trade test.
- Usable scope: Nondegenerate current-window enhanced profile/POC. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Lookback, bin count, Gaussian sigma, maximum cluster centers, pivot length, retained profiles and display width. Default maximum clusters is two.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Close-only allocation and smoothing can move apparent volume concentrations away from executed-price distribution.
- Flat ranges, no qualifying peaks and tied bins require implementation choices; historical swing confirmation also introduces delay.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Pivot confirmation, empty-cluster fallback, endpoint/tie behavior and historical segment inclusion rules are not supplied.

## Data requirements

Visualize cryptocurrency open-interest changes by intrabar price level. The footprint labels opening/closing behavior inferred from price direction and OI change, making it a positioning proxy rather than direct observation of which participant initiated a trade.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Four nonzero price/OI sign labels is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Retrieve lower-timeframe price ranges, direction and OI changes. Rising price with rising OI is labeled longs opening; rising price/falling OI shorts closing; falling price/rising OI shorts opening; falling price/falling OI longs closing.
- Aggregate categories into footprint price levels, either resetting each bar or accumulating until a selected reset boundary. Delta and percentage overlays summarize net change.
- A value-area/POC view highlights concentration. Level delta exceeding a selected imbalance percentage produces markers; consecutive imbalanced levels trigger an alert.
- Given synchronized nonzero price/OI changes classify(+,+)=UU longs opening,(+,-)=UD shorts closing,(-,+)=DU shorts opening,(-,-)=DD longs closing. These reproduce heuristic labels,not true participant identification. Zero cases,footprint rows,delta percentages/value area remain outside scope;external OI is still required.

## Outputs and intended use

- Boxes display delta, delta percentage and inferred long/short opening/closing categories, with category or simple up/down colors.
- The author suggests absorption/exhaustion and entry-context use; chart data does not verify those causal interpretations.
- Usable scope: Four nonzero price/OI sign labels. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- One-minute, one-second or one-tick granularity; manual tick spacing or zero for ATR-based automatic spacing.
- Cumulative/reset timeframe, value-area percentage, imbalance threshold/count and visibility/colors.

## Failure modes and caveats

- An OI increase creates both a long and short contract; direction-based attribution cannot uniquely identify longs or shorts opening.
- Tick/second histories and OI timestamps may have different coverage. Signed changes also make a percentage-containing value area ambiguous.

## Idea and objective

Earnings Snapshot organizes historical stock EPS releases, future estimates and associated price growth into a chart table and release-date labels. It replaces manual comparisons of quarterly reports with a compact view of growth and price reaction. Revenue is expressly excluded because the author had not resolved its data presentation. This is fundamental-event visualization rather than an alerting or backtesting system; a favorable color should not be treated as an independently verified earnings beat or trading recommendation.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow historical actual-EPS growth: given ordered quarterly actual EPS E_q, calculate Q2Q=100×(E_q/E_(q−1)−1) and Y2Y=100×(E_q/E_(q−4)−1), restricted to positive comparison bases. Use four reported quarterly observations back, not inferred calendar-year alignment. Price-growth and future-estimate score components are separate.
- Retrieve actual, estimated and standardized EPS and compare earnings and prices with the preceding quarter and four quarters earlier.
- For each comparison add or subtract one for positive earnings growth, positive price growth and earnings growth exceeding price growth; repeat for year-over-year and add the future-estimate direction.

## Outputs and intended use

- Show complete text or compact score labels with hover details, plus an optional growth table.
- Review slowing growth, price/earnings divergence and upcoming estimate direction around earnings dates.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Seven factors produce scores from -7 to +7. Historical lookback reaches 24 quarters.
- Display mode, label size and table visibility are configurable.
- Use supplied ordered actual quarterly EPS; quarter lags are one and four, with strictly positive bases for this narrow standard percentage-change calculation. Zero/negative EPS, irregular reporting and release/revision timing remain caveats.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Quarter-based indexing assumes regular reporting and may misalign irregular issuers.
- Negative or zero EPS bases complicate percentage-growth interpretation.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Price sampling at earnings events, zero/negative-denominator handling and future-estimate feed timing are not specified.

## Idea and objective

Provide strategy programmers with unit conversions, direction-aware exit levels, risk-based size helpers and a percentage-exit wrapper. These functions support a caller’s existing strategy and do not define an entry edge.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Percentage conversions use average entry price or an explicit price; tick conversions connect instrument price units and currency amounts. Profit calculation evaluates a hypothetical exit relative to the active position.
- Stop and target helpers offset average entry by ticks and reverse direction for short positions. Position-size helpers target a fixed equity percentage using stop distance.
- exitPercent wraps a strategy exit with percentage loss/profit arguments and optional absolute or percentage exit quantities.
- For supplied price P and percentage p,percent amount=P*p/100. For supplied average entry E,tick size q,distance d>=0 and side s=+1 long/-1 short,stop=E-s*d*q,target=E+s*d*q. These helpers qualify independently from sizing rounding,currency/point-value conversions,absent-position behavior and pyramiding-sensitive exit wrapper.

## Outputs and intended use

- Returns ticks, price/currency values, percentage profit, stop/target levels and integer contract counts.
- The demonstration plots entry, stop and target levels and marks trades; levels may be passed into the caller’s exit orders.
- Usable scope: Percent-of-price and signed tick exit-level helpers. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Stop distance in ticks or percentage, equity risk percentage, entry/exit prices, order identifier, quantities, conditions and alert text.
- For exitPercent, qty defaults to na and the percentage quantity defaults to 100 when absolute quantity is absent.

## Failure modes and caveats

- The author warns that average-entry offsets may work incorrectly with pyramiding.
- Tick/currency/contract conversions need instrument point value, rounding and account currency treatment; incorrect assumptions would change risk. Stops do not guarantee realized loss during gaps.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

# Simplified Percentile Clustering

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Simplified Percentile Clustering creates deterministic regime centers from percentiles and a mean instead of iterative k-means. It can classify one indicator or fuse several normalized indicators by their distances to corresponding centers, then interpolate toward the next closest regime. This is a clustering heuristic for interpreting market state, explicitly not a buy/sell model or forecast.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Standalone percentile centers/distance interpolation is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Build low/high centers halfway between lower/upper percentiles and mean, adding the mean as a middle center when selected.
- Average distances across enabled RSI/CCI/Fisher/DMI/Z-score/price-to-MA features and choose the closest combined center.
- Interpolate nearest and second-nearest cluster values using their distance ratio to show proximity transitions.
- For supplied feature/window compute low_pct,high_pct and mean mid. K=2 centers=((low_pct+mid)/2,(high_pct+mid)/2);K=3 adds mid between them. Given distances d1,d2 to the closest and second-closest feature-space centers, and their assigned cluster label/index values c1,c2,rel_pos=d1/(d1+d2);real_clust=c1+(c2-c1)*rel_pos. The interpolated output is in cluster label/index units, not feature-space centroid magnitudes. Require nonzero distance sum;feature fusion and normalization remain excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect colored regime histograms, bar colors and continuous transition line; use as an interpretable research feature or adaptive-filter context.
- Usable scope: Standalone percentile centers/distance interpolation. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Two or three clusters are supported; lookback, percentile cutoffs and feature toggles/standardization are configurable without full defaults.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: correlated features receive repeated influence, standardization choices alter distance and the prose’s 0/0.5/1 transition interpretation does not directly follow its nearest-distance ratio.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Feature variants/lengths, exact distance metric, normalization, tie behavior and zero-enabled-feature handling are not fully specified.

# Sharpe and Sortino Ratios

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** reporting-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Evaluate risk-adjusted price-return performance relative to a fixed annual benchmark or an aligned comparison asset.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for periodic Sharpe and active-return information ratios with supplied aligned samples and caller dispersion/zero conventions; annual conversion and Sortino parity remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- For supplied same-period returns r and periodic risk-free return f, Sharpe=(mean(r)-f)/SD(r). For aligned investment/benchmark returns r,b, information ratio=mean(r-b)/SD(r-b). Caller must select sample/population dispersion and zero-dispersion policy because the description does not fix them. These periodic formulas avoid guessing annual-to-period conversion.
- Request chosen-timeframe percentage changes,compound them into monthly samples when history spans two months or daily samples when it spans two days,and compute excess mean divided by total/downside dispersion. Benchmark-symbol mode uses active-return/tracking-error style ratios with aligned spread requests and dividend/extended-session adjustments.

## Outputs and intended use

- Display return series,benchmark line,new-period highlights and a table/data-window of ratios/sample information. These describe asset price returns,not an actual trading portfolio.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Returns timeframe defaults one month,maximum samples sixty and annual fixed benchmark two percent. Less than two days produces no collected returns. Benchmark choice/timeframe/sample count are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Yield-valued symbols are unsuitable price-return benchmarks,as the author warns. Results depend on sampling,adjustments and downside convention; a high historical ratio does not establish future sustainability.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact annual-to-period conversion,downside-deviation denominator/zero cases,partial-period compounding and benchmark request mappings require the RiskMetrics library/code.

Required inputs: chart price history, manual annual benchmark or aligned benchmark-price series.

# Range Oscillator (Zeiierman)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Range Oscillator expresses the distance of the closing price from an adaptive equilibrium as a percentage of a volatility-adjusted range. Its heatmap is intended to distinguish directional pressure, transition areas and excursions beyond an ordinary range. The author offers both breakout and mean-reversion interpretations, so an extreme does not carry a single unambiguous trading instruction. The normalizing equation is disclosed, but the adaptive inputs and color engine remain substantially descriptive.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** Core computation remains underspecified.

- RangeATR construction, weighted mean and heatmap computations are missing.

## How it works

- Detect a range using a minimum confirmation length and ATR width multiplier.
- Weight the equilibrium mean by consecutive candle-movement size, then compute 100 times close minus mean divided by RangeATR.
- Assign adaptive heat colors according to interaction intensity, heat levels and minimum touches.

## Outputs and intended use

- Above-zero green readings suggest bullish pressure and below-zero red readings bearish pressure.
- Excursions beyond +100 or -100 prompt breakout/exhaustion assessment; movement back toward zero suggests a possible range reset.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Minimum range length, ATR width multiplier, number of heat levels and minimum touches are configurable; numeric defaults are absent.

## Failure modes and caveats

- The same excursion can precede continuation or reversal; colors do not determine which will occur.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Weighted-mean formula, ATR period, range confirmation/reset and touch-counting color thresholds are undefined.

# Geo.

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** financial-library. Native publication type: library. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Geo supplies reusable geometry for chart-based price analysis and drawings. Its worked example constructs points from bar indices and closing/opening prices, builds a sloping line and suggests detecting a crossing for an alert, giving the otherwise general mathematics an explicit financial application.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for nondegenerate supplied-anchor line geometry and chart-price comparisons; safeindex, degenerate lines and specialized arc/spiral/hull implementations remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- For nondegenerate supplied price/bar-index anchors (x1,y1),(x2,y2), standard documented slope is m=(y2-y1)/(x2-x1), and gety(x)=y1+m*(x-x1). With m!=0, getx(y)=x1+(y-y1)/m. For two nonparallel lines y=m1*x+b1 and y=m2*x+b2, intersection x=(b2-b1)/(m1-m2), y=m1*x+b1. Comparing chart price with gety(bar index) supports the suggested crossing use case. These equations spell out standard meanings of the documented primitives, not unseen implementation code.
- Point stores coordinates plus auxiliary angle and value fields; Line stores an anchor point and slope. Functions manipulate coordinates through arithmetic, rotations, vector products, normalization and projections, then calculate line coordinates or intersections.
- Point-array methods support coordinate averages and ranges, sorting and polygon operations, including area, perimeter, containment and convex hulls. Separate spiral/arc helpers estimate centers, edge coordinates and growth factors. Conversion methods translate the custom Point representation into chart points before drawing lines.

## Outputs and intended use

- Consumers receive scalar distances/angles, transformed points, intersections, point arrays and chart line objects. These primitives can support price geometry or alert conditions chosen by the caller; the library itself does not specify a trading signal.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Functions accept caller-provided points, slopes, scalars, angles, polygon vertices and drawing styles. Rotation interfaces distinguish radians from degrees. The example uses bar_index and close for one point and bar_index[2] and open for another.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Mixing bar-index and price units makes geometric distances and angles scale dependent. Degenerate vectors, vertical/parallel lines and malformed polygons require explicit handling before use.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- The description gives interfaces and many standard operations but omits implementation and edge policies for specialized arc, spiral and hull routines. Some generated documentation conflicts: min_y describes x coordinates, and perimeter describes both a perimeter and an array hull return.
- safeindex conversion policy and vertical/parallel/zero-slope handling are not specified; the narrow equations apply only on nondegenerate domains.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv.

# Relative Volume at Time

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Relative Volume at Time compares current participation with historical participation at the same offset inside a chosen time unit. It addresses recurring intraday or weekly volume cycles that an ordinary rolling average can obscure. Users can compare either cumulative activity since the anchor or a single matched-offset bar. The normalized result supports comparisons across markets, while the directional variant signs volume by bar direction rather than claiming to observe actual buying and selling.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** The main relative-volume calculation and parameterized variants are explicitly defined.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Divide cumulative volume since a unit begins by the mean cumulative volume through the same offset in prior units; alternatively divide one bar by the mean of matching-offset prior bars.
- Select automatic, fixed or time-of-day anchors. Automatic units step from minute/hour/day through week/month/year according to chart resolution.
- Apply Hull smoothing, optional sign by up/down bar, and fixed, mean-plus/minus-standard-deviation or historical high/low thresholds.

## Outputs and intended use

- Display raw/current versus historical columns, relative columns, smoothed relative volume or signed relative volume.
- Color-state transitions create markers and alerts; the source leaves the individual eight selectable conditions unnamed.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Fixed threshold defaults to 2.0; fixed channel lookback defaults to 100.
- Lookbacks exceeding 5000 chart bars are adjusted; only the latest 500 value labels display.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Realtime volume is incomplete until bar close. Daily and intraday feeds can disagree.
- Volume alone has no price direction or guarantee of substantial movement.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Eight optional coloring predicates, missing-offset handling and zero-volume denominator handling are not enumerated; these do not prevent the core matched-volume computation.

# Asset Drift Model

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Asset Drift Model tests whether historical returns support a persistent directional bias rather than reacting to the latest price swing. It combines mean-return inference with economic-size, power, sign consistency, subsample stability and mean-reversion checks. The output distinguishes strong, weak or absent evidence, making no-evidence a failure to establish drift rather than proof of randomness. Its role is retrospective regime and portfolio research. Several prose claims overstate what small samples or absent drift establish; a zero mean does not imply random-walk behavior, and non-overlapping returns are not automatically independent.

- HAC, minimum-detectable-effect, sign-test and variance-ratio equations are missing.

## How it works

- Form non-overlapping log returns and estimate mean drift with a simplified one-lag HAC standard error.
- Check sign-test evidence, mean/median agreement, half-sample consistency and variance-ratio mean reversion.
- Require significance, effect size, stated detectability and robustness for strong evidence; report rejection reasons otherwise.

## Outputs and intended use

- Dashboard shows directional/evidence class, sample status, t statistics, MDE/power, sign/stability/variance-ratio diagnostics and annualized drift.

- Uses 60-day returns over 756 trading days, described as 12 full-sample and six half-sample observations.
- Absolute t threshold 2.0, economic threshold 3% annualized and sign-test annotation at 10%.

## Failure modes and caveats

- The default sample is explicitly in the heuristic range; asymptotic significance labels are uncertain.
- Comparing observed effect with an MDE is not a complete power analysis without a specified power target.
- Historical drift can change and does not establish net long/short edge.

# RedK Compound Ratio Moving Average (CoRa_Wave)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

CoRa Wave gives more recent observations geometrically increasing weights to create a responsive moving average. Its aim is to reduce the influence of the oldest observations while retaining a finite-window average that can be used for trend and swing tracking. An accelerator changes how aggressively weights favor recent prices, and optional smoothing moderates the response. The author proposes crossover use, including equal-length lines on open and close, but provides no full trading system. Low-lag language describes intent and examples rather than a measured guarantee.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for a parameterized geometric-weight moving average using disclosed compound-ratio equations with caller-chosen endpoints/window. Actual endpoint defaults, accelerator and automatic/manual smoothing remain outside the usable scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Independent unaccelerated, unsmoothed geometric-weight MA: choose positive start weight P, endpoint A and t weight steps. Compute r=(A/P)^(1/t)−1; index the oldest sample as j=0 and set w_j=P×(1+r)^j. Return sum(w_j×source_j)/sum(w_j) over the selected window. This is a normalized weighted average using the disclosed weight sequence, not a reconstruction of undocumented accelerator/smoothing defaults.
- Apply an accelerator to emphasize recent observations and optional automatic/manual smoothing.

## Outputs and intended use

- A price-tracking MA supports trend observation or caller-defined crossovers.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Default resolution is chart timeframe and source hlc3.
- Multiplier zero produces SMA; source says effects are strongest around 1–5 then diminish.
- Example comparison length is 20; actual length/smoothing defaults are absent.
- Narrow geometric-weight scope requires chosen window, positive endpoint weights P and A, with t the number of weight steps; the source gives no endpoint defaults. Disable added acceleration and smoothing for this scope.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Greater recent-price weighting increases sensitivity to noise.
- The prose’s contrast with EMA should not be read as proof of uniquely geometric weighting or universal lag reduction.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Start/end weight choices, exact accelerator/smoothing formulas, confirmation timing and entry/exit rules are absent.

# CVD - Cumulative Volume Delta Candles

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Cumulative Volume Delta Candles approximates directional volume from intrabars and displays its accumulated path as candles. It aims to expose within-bar pressure and longer reset-period progression more precisely than assigning each whole chart candle a single sign. Users can compare CVD direction, wicks and price disagreement, while choosing a precision/history tradeoff. The method remains an approximation rather than bid/ask transaction classification. Reset choices define independent analysis chunks, so a trend across a reset cannot be interpreted as uninterrupted accumulated flow.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Intrabar direction and flat-bar fallback, signed-volume aggregation, candle open/close and configurable reset modes define the principal CVD computation. Exact automatic precision selection is an optional data-selection caveat.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Sign intrabar volume by close versus open; for dojis use previous intrabar close, then last known polarity if still unchanged.
- Sum signed intrabars for each chart-bar delta and accumulate through the reset period.
- Build candle open from prior CVD close, close from aggregate delta and wicks from intrabar delta extremes.

## Outputs and intended use

- CVD candles, optional total-intrabar-volume candles, divergence coloring, reset background and LTF/coverage information box support flow analysis.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Reset choices: none, fixed HTF, fixed time, regular-session start or stepped HTF.
- Stepped mapping is sub-minute→1H, below 3H→1D, at most 12H→1W, below 1W→1M, otherwise 1Y.
- Precision options range from broad coverage to one-minute intrabars; total-volume candles default off.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Intraday/EOD and realtime/historical volume feeds can differ.
- Finer intrabars reduce historical chart coverage; missing activity affects totals.
- Candle polarity does not measure actual aggressor-side volume.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact LTF selection, reset default/timezone, intrabar-extreme construction and trade rules are absent.

## Idea and objective

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- From the two-year price-high anchor, sum daily short-sale volume S and total volume V and calculate S/V. Color the connecting line red when S/V >= 20% and green otherwise. The numerator measures transaction flow, not outstanding short positions.
- For a new one-year short-volume high, aggregate the five preceding sessions, event session and four following sessions. For a price pivot defined as the highest high over 51 sessions, aggregate three preceding sessions, the event and two following sessions. Calculate short/total-volume ratios over those retrospective windows and apply the same color threshold.
- Secondary dollar estimates use VWAP with short and non-short turnover, but the exact VWAP anchoring is not defined.

## Outputs and intended use

- Labels, boxes and lines compare short-volume ratios around events. The text calls one measure short interest ratio, but its described numerator is short-sale volume, not outstanding short positions.

## Parameters and stated settings

- The threshold is twenty percent. The price pivot spans 51 sessions. Short-volume-high windows contain five preceding, the event and four subsequent sessions; price-pivot windows contain three preceding, the event and two subsequent sessions.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Both event windows include future sessions, so finalized stamps are retrospective. VWAP times turnover estimates gross transaction value and cannot establish remaining short positions.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Short-volume feed, handling of future-window completion, overlapping events, universe coverage and exact VWAP anchoring are omitted.

## Idea and objective

First Passage Time Distribution Analysis simulates when price might first reach user-defined upper or lower percentage targets. It separates time-to-target summaries from which boundary is reached first, making it a scenario tool for holding-period and risk planning. Its estimates are conditional on a geometric-Brownian-motion model fitted to recent history; the source expressly notes that it runs only on the last bar and does not provide historical signals.

## How it works

- Estimate drift and log-return volatility, annualize them and simulate GBM paths.
- Track first threshold hits, aggregate first-hit direction probabilities and summarize target times with percentiles, mean and median.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect threshold lines, risk zones and a statistics table when evaluating targets, stops or time horizons; these are model scenarios, not option-assignment probabilities.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Source describes over 1,000 paths. Distribution percentiles are 10/25/50/75/90, with optional one/two-sigma display.
- Historical drift is default, with zero drift and half-drift scenarios available; threshold size and simulation horizon defaults are not disclosed.

# Time & volume point of control / Flowly Indicators

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Show where each candle's strongest time occupancy and volume concentration occurred using lower-timeframe approximations.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** The lower-timeframe selection map, maximum-volume source-price rule and ten-bracket close-count TPOC rule are explicitly stated. Tie handling is a nonblocking edge convention.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Choose the lower-timeframe bar with greatest volume and mark its selected price as VPOC. Divide the parent candle into ten price lots, count lower-timeframe closes in each and mark the midpoint of the most occupied lot as TPOC.

## Outputs and intended use

- Plot time as a line and volume as a dot, optionally replacing ordinary candle bodies with a range line. Concentration-threshold colors emphasize dominant observations. Suggested trapped-participant/trend narratives remain interpretations.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Default lower-timeframe map: chart <=30 minutes uses 1 minute; >30 minutes through 3 hours uses 5 minutes; >3 through 8 hours uses 15 minutes; >8 hours through 1 day uses 1 hour; >1 through 3 days uses 2 hours; >3 days uses 4 hours.
- Price source defaults to lower-timeframe close. Users can change source, interval and concentration thresholds. TPOC divides each candle range into ten price lots.

## Failure modes and caveats

- This VPOC is the price of the highest-volume sub-bar, not necessarily the true most-traded price. Finer data improves granularity but reduces accessible history and slows loading.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Tie resolution, missing sub-bars and exact treatment of boundary-equal closes are not supplied. No portfolio entry/exit process is specified.

# Detrended Rhythm Oscillator (DRO)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Detrended Rhythm Oscillator makes cycle inspection easier by marking turns in detrended price and labeling distances between comparable turns. It is designed to identify recurring or harmonic intervals that could tune other indicators, not to predict an exact next turning point. The extra detrended-zigzag display removes amplitude differences so timing patterns are easier to see.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** DPO offset/window, zigzag reversal threshold, amplitude-detrending transform and pivot confirmation are unspecified.

- DPO offset/window, zigzag reversal threshold, amplitude-detrending transform and pivot confirmation are unspecified.

## How it works

- Detrend price with DPO, find turns with zigzag, remove zigzag amplitude and measure high-to-high/low-to-low pivot bar distances.

## Outputs and intended use

- Look for repeated distances and harmonic relationships, then use an investigated cycle estimate as another indicator’s parameter; source discourages direct turn forecasting.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Example distances cluster around 40/80/120 bars. Display options include DPO, zigzag/DRO, detrended zigzag and length labels; no numerical calculation defaults are supplied.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: zigzag turning points require later information, and apparent harmonic clusters can arise from threshold selection or chance.
